title: Lucyyx Never Clear
statementMd:
We define the function F(N,M)𝐹(𝑁,𝑀) to be the number of ordered pairs of integers (a,b) such that 1≤a≤N, 1≤b≤M, and gcd(agcd(a,b),b)=gcd(a,b).

You are given that F(3,3)=7, F(10,103)=6947, and F(105,103)=69278063.

Find F(n,m) modulo 998244353.

## Input

The first and only line contains two integers n and m (1≤n,m≤1010) — the values for which you must calculate F(n,m).

## Output

Output a single integer — the value F(n,m) modulo 998244353.

## Note

In the first test case, we have that gcd(3gcd(3,1),1)=1=gcd(3,1), so (3,1) is counted as a valid ordered pair. We also have that gcd(2gcd(2,2),2)=1≠2=gcd(2,2), so (2,2) is not counted as a valid ordered pair. The 7 valid ordered pairs are (1,1),(1,2),(1,3),(2,1),(2,3),(3,1), and (3,2).
